sections.body: This field applies artificial intelligence to the internal legal and compliance work of companies. It includes advising boards on fiduciary risk, auditing supply chains and sustainability claims, detecting insider trading and market abuse, mapping regulatory change, and modelling mergers. The tools do not replace lawyers or compliance officers. They read large volumes of contracts, filings, trading data, and regulatory text to flag patterns that a person would then review. The work is operational, not advisory in the sense of giving a final legal opinion.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some tasks are more mature than others. Insider trading detection is closest to solved because it relies on well understood statistical anomaly detection over market and communications data. Regulatory change mapping is reliable for tracking text changes but still struggles with interpreting how a new rule changes a company's obligations. Board advisory and merger modelling remain assistive, not autonomous, because they require judgment about fiduciary duties and deal structure. The honest limit is that these systems produce candidates and summaries, not decisions. The site tracks 6823 state AI bills, which gives a sense of the volume of regulatory text that mapping tools must process, and 210 compliance and regulation pages that document the current rules.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking at director duties would start with Board Advisory and Fiduciary Risk, which covers how AI flags conflicts and oversight gaps. Supply Chain and Sustainability Auditing explains how models check supplier contracts and emissions reports against stated ESG commitments. Insider Trading and Market Abuse Detection describes the surveillance patterns used for unusual trades or communications before announcements. Regulatory Change Mapping shows how new statutes and agency rules are matched to affected business units. Merger and Restructuring Analysis covers the modelling of deal terms, synergies, and post merger compliance risks. Together the pages move from the boardroom outward to supply chains, markets, regulators, and finally the structure of the company itself.
